data.title: B1 Progress Check
data.description: A second mixed grammar check to measure progress and confirm whether the learner is working securely at CEFR B1 level.

sections.explain: Use the past perfect ('had' + participle) for the earlier past action: 'had started'. 'has started' is present perfect, and 'had start' lacks the participle.

words.word: When I arrived, the meeting had already started.
When I arrived, the meeting has already started.
When I arrived, the meeting had already start.

sections.explain: 'What' is the subject here, so no auxiliary 'did' is used: 'What happened?'. 'What did happen/happened' incorrectly adds 'did'.

words.word: What happened at the meeting?
What did happened at the meeting?
What did happen at the meeting?

sections.explain: Names of oceans take 'the': 'the Atlantic'. Omitting the article or using 'an' with a specific ocean name is wrong.

words.word: We sailed across an Atlantic.
We sailed across the Atlantic.
We sailed across Atlantic.

sections.explain: Use an adverb to describe how an action is done: 'sang beautifully'. The adjective 'beautiful' describes nouns, not verbs.

words.word: She sang the song more beautiful.
She sang the song beautiful.
She sang the song beautifully.

sections.explain: The future continuous ('will be' + -ing) describes an action in progress at a future time: 'will be flying'. 'will be fly' lacks the -ing form.

words.word: This time tomorrow, I will been flying to Rome.
This time tomorrow, I will be fly to Rome.
This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Rome.

sections.explain: For a negative deduction, use 'can't be': 'He can't be at home'. 'mustn't' means prohibition, not deduction, and modals take no 'to'.

words.word: He can't to be at home; his car isn't here.
He mustn't be at home; his car isn't here.
He can't be at home; his car isn't here.

sections.explain: 'Although' introduces a contrast clause and is not paired with 'but'. 'Despite' is followed by a noun/-ing, not a full clause.

words.word: Despite it was raining, we went out.
Although it was raining, we went out.
Although it was raining, but we went out.

sections.explain: We 'make a decision' in English: it is a fixed collocation. 'do a decision' and 'have a decision' are not standard.

words.word: I need to do a decision quickly.
I need to make a decision quickly.
I need to have a decision quickly.

sections.explain: The noun form of 'explain' is 'explanation': 'Her explanation was clear'. 'explain' is the verb, and 'explanating' is not a word.

words.word: Her explanation was very clear.
Her explain was very clear.
Her explanating was very clear.

sections.explain: 'Nevertheless' links two sentences to show contrast and stands alone: 'Nevertheless, we will try it'. 'Nevertheless of this' and 'However that' are not correct forms.

words.word: The plan is risky. Nevertheless, we will try it.
The plan is risky. However that, we will try it.
The plan is risky. Nevertheless of this, we will try it.
